title: Mycology II
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 400L Botany/Plant Science Mycology II curriculum, building on introductory Mycology I: advanced fungal classification (Ascomycota, Basidiomycota, higher fungal groups), fungal life cycles and sexual/asexual reproduction, fungal genetics and heterokaryosis, economic and industrial mycology, fungal plant pathogens and disease cycles, mycorrhizae and lichens, and fungal ecology/decomposition. Distinct from introductory Mycology I, which covers general fungal structure, nutrition and lower fungal groups.

questions.question: Members of the phylum Ascomycota are characterised primarily by the production of sexual spores called:
questions.correct_answer: Ascospores
questions.explanation: Ascomycetes produce sexual spores (ascospores), typically eight, within a sac-like structure called an ascus, following karyogamy and meiosis.

questions.question: In Ascomycota, the fruiting body that is a closed, spherical structure with asci embedded inside and no natural opening is called a:
questions.correct_answer: Cleistothecium
questions.explanation: A cleistothecium is a completely closed ascocarp; asci and ascospores are released only when the wall ruptures or decays, distinguishing it from the perithecium (flask-shaped, with an ostiole) and the open, cup-shaped apothecium.

questions.question: The flask-shaped ascocarp with a small opening (ostiole) through which ascospores are released is called a:
questions.correct_answer: Perithecium
questions.explanation: A perithecium is a flask-shaped fruiting body with an ostiole at the apex allowing ascospore discharge, common in fungi such as Neurospora and Sordaria.

questions.question: Which of the following genera is a classic Ascomycete model organism widely used in fungal genetics because of its ordered tetrad/octad analysis?
questions.correct_answer: Neurospora crassa
questions.explanation: Neurospora crassa's linear arrangement of ascospores within the ascus permits ordered tetrad analysis, making it a foundational model organism for fungal genetics, including the 'one gene-one enzyme' work of Beadle and Tatum.

questions.question: Basidiomycota are characterised by production of sexual spores called basidiospores, typically borne externally on a club-shaped structure called a:
questions.correct_answer: Basidium
questions.explanation: In Basidiomycota, karyogamy and meiosis occur within the basidium, and the resulting haploid basidiospores are borne externally, typically four per basidium, on sterigmata.

questions.question: The dikaryotic stage (n+n), in which two genetically distinct haploid nuclei coexist in a common cytoplasm without fusing, is especially prolonged and prominent in the life cycle of:
questions.correct_answer: Basidiomycota
questions.explanation: Basidiomycetes have an extended dikaryotic (n+n) mycelial phase, formed after plasmogamy via clamp connections, that can persist for a long time before eventual karyogamy in the basidium.

questions.question: Clamp connections, distinctive hyphal structures found in many Basidiomycota, function to:
options: Ensure that each dikaryotic cell formed during hyphal growth retains one nucleus of each mating type
Anchor the fungus to its substrate
questions.correct_answer: Ensure that each dikaryotic cell formed during hyphal growth retains one nucleus of each mating type
questions.explanation: Clamp connections are bridge-like structures that maintain the dikaryotic condition by ensuring correct nuclear distribution to daughter cells during hyphal septation and division.

questions.question: Heterokaryosis in fungi refers to a condition in which:
options: A single hyphal compartment or mycelium contains two or more genetically different nuclei
All nuclei in the mycelium are genetically identical
questions.correct_answer: A single hyphal compartment or mycelium contains two or more genetically different nuclei
questions.explanation: Heterokaryosis arises from hyphal fusion (anastomosis) between genetically distinct mycelia, producing cells with genetically different nuclei sharing common cytoplasm, an important source of variation in fungi lacking a regular sexual cycle.

questions.question: The parasexual cycle in fungi (important in organisms lacking a regular sexual cycle, e.g. many Deuteromycetes) generates genetic variation through:
options: Nuclear fusion in a heterokaryon followed by mitotic recombination and progressive haploidisation, without meiosis
questions.correct_answer: Nuclear fusion in a heterokaryon followed by mitotic recombination and progressive haploidisation, without meiosis
questions.explanation: The parasexual cycle involves occasional fusion of unlike nuclei in a heterokaryon to form a diploid, followed by mitotic crossing-over and gradual chromosome loss back to the haploid state, generating recombinant genotypes without a true meiotic sexual cycle.

questions.question: Fungi historically grouped as 'Deuteromycetes' or 'Fungi Imperfecti' are so named because:
options: They lack any known sexual (teleomorphic) reproductive stage
questions.correct_answer: They lack any known sexual (teleomorphic) reproductive stage
questions.explanation: Deuteromycetes (Fungi Imperfecti) reproduce only asexually (anamorphic state) as far as is known; many have since been reclassified into Ascomycota or Basidiomycota once their sexual (teleomorph) stage was discovered.

questions.question: Puccinia graminis, the causal agent of wheat/cereal stem rust, is notable for having a life cycle with how many distinct spore stages, often on two different host plants (heteroecious)?
questions.correct_answer: Five
questions.explanation: Puccinia graminis has a complex heteroecious life cycle with five spore stages (pycniospores, aeciospores on barberry, urediniospores and teliospores on cereals, and basidiospores), a classic example of rust fungus complexity.

questions.question: A heteroecious rust fungus requires:
options: Two taxonomically unrelated host species to complete its full life cycle
No host at all, being fully saprophytic
questions.correct_answer: Two taxonomically unrelated host species to complete its full life cycle
questions.explanation: Heteroecious rusts alternate between two unrelated host plants to complete different stages of their life cycle, e.g. Puccinia graminis alternates between cereals and barberry.

questions.question: Smut fungi (order Ustilaginales, Basidiomycota) characteristically cause plant disease symptoms involving:
options: Formation of masses of dark, powdery teliospores replacing host reproductive/floral tissues such as grains
questions.correct_answer: Formation of masses of dark, powdery teliospores replacing host reproductive/floral tissues such as grains
questions.explanation: Smuts characteristically replace host tissues, especially cereal grains/inflorescences, with dark masses of thick-walled teliospores that resemble soot, hence the common name.

questions.question: A disease cycle in plant pathology refers to:
options: The sequence of events involved in disease development, from inoculation through infection, colonisation, and reproduction/spread of the pathogen
The life cycle of the host plant alone
A single infection event with no further spread
The taxonomic classification of the pathogen
questions.correct_answer: The sequence of events involved in disease development, from inoculation through infection, colonisation, and reproduction/spread of the pathogen
questions.explanation: The disease cycle describes the chronological stages -- inoculation, penetration, infection, incubation, symptom expression, and spore/inoculum production and dispersal -- through which a pathogen causes and perpetuates disease.

questions.question: Mycorrhizae are symbiotic associations between fungi and:
questions.correct_answer: Plant roots
questions.explanation: Mycorrhizae are mutualistic symbioses between fungi and the roots of the great majority of vascular plants, improving mineral and water uptake for the plant in exchange for photosynthate.

questions.question: Ectomycorrhizal fungi differ from arbuscular (endo-) mycorrhizal fungi mainly in that ectomycorrhizae:
options: Form a hyphal sheath (mantle) around the root and a Hartig net between cortical cells, without penetrating the cells themselves
Penetrate directly into root cortical cells, forming arbuscules
questions.correct_answer: Form a hyphal sheath (mantle) around the root and a Hartig net between cortical cells, without penetrating the cells themselves
questions.explanation: Ectomycorrhizae (common in many tree families) form an external mantle and intercellular Hartig net without entering host cells, whereas arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi penetrate cortical cells to form intracellular arbuscules.

questions.question: A lichen is best described as:
options: A single fungal species growing independently
A symbiotic association between a fungus (mycobiont) and a photosynthetic partner (alga or cyanobacterium, the photobiont)
A purely parasitic relationship that kills the photosynthetic partner rapidly
questions.correct_answer: A symbiotic association between a fungus (mycobiont) and a photosynthetic partner (alga or cyanobacterium, the photobiont)
questions.explanation: A lichen is a stable mutualistic (or controlled parasitic) symbiosis in which the fungal partner provides structure and protection while the photobiont supplies fixed carbon through photosynthesis.

questions.question: Based on growth form, lichens are commonly classified into crustose, foliose and fruticose types. A fruticose lichen has a growth form that is:
options: Flat and tightly adhering to the substrate like a crust
Leaf-like, with a lower and upper surface loosely attached to the substrate
Shrubby or bushy, and free-standing or hanging
questions.correct_answer: Shrubby or bushy, and free-standing or hanging
questions.explanation: Fruticose lichens have a three-dimensional, shrub-like or pendant growth form, distinguished from the flat, tightly attached crustose form and the leaf-like foliose form.

questions.question: Lichens are widely used as bioindicators of environmental quality mainly because they are:
options: Highly sensitive to air pollution, particularly sulphur dioxide
Completely insensitive to any environmental change
Only found in heavily polluted cities
Immune to all forms of stress
questions.correct_answer: Highly sensitive to air pollution, particularly sulphur dioxide
questions.explanation: Lichens absorb substances directly from the atmosphere and lack a protective cuticle, making them highly sensitive to air pollutants like SO2; their diversity and abundance are used to monitor air quality.

questions.question: Which of the following fungi is of major industrial/economic importance as the source organism for penicillin antibiotic production?
questions.correct_answer: Penicillium chrysogenum
questions.explanation: Penicillium chrysogenum (and related Penicillium species) is industrially cultured to produce penicillin, one of the most important antibiotics discovered from a fungal secondary metabolite.

questions.question: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (baker's/brewer's yeast) is economically important mainly for its role in:
options: Alcoholic fermentation and leavening of bread through carbon dioxide production
questions.correct_answer: Alcoholic fermentation and leavening of bread through carbon dioxide production
questions.explanation: S. cerevisiae ferments sugars to ethanol and CO2, which is exploited in brewing/winemaking (ethanol) and baking (CO2 for leavening), making it one of the most economically important fungi.

questions.question: Aspergillus niger is widely used industrially for the commercial production of:
questions.correct_answer: Citric acid
questions.explanation: Aspergillus niger is the principal organism used in industrial fermentation to produce citric acid, an important commodity in the food and beverage industry.

questions.question: Aflatoxins, dangerous carcinogenic mycotoxins that contaminate stored groundnuts, maize and other crops in Nigeria, are produced mainly by species of:
questions.correct_answer: Aspergillus (A. flavus and A. parasiticus)
questions.explanation: Aflatoxins are potent hepatotoxic and carcinogenic secondary metabolites produced mainly by Aspergillus flavus and A. parasiticus growing on improperly stored grains and nuts under warm, humid conditions -- a significant food safety concern in Nigeria.

questions.question: Mushroom cultivation (e.g. of Agaricus bisporus or Pleurotus species) as a food source is an example of:
options: Beneficial economic mycology / edible fungi utilisation
An entirely parasitic relationship harming humans
A method of fungal disease control
questions.correct_answer: Beneficial economic mycology / edible fungi utilisation
questions.explanation: Cultivated edible mushrooms such as Agaricus bisporus (button mushroom) and Pleurotus species (oyster mushroom) are grown commercially for food, representing an important area of applied/economic mycology.

questions.question: In fungal ecology, saprophytic (saprotrophic) fungi obtain nutrients by:
options: Decomposing dead organic matter and absorbing the released nutrients
questions.correct_answer: Decomposing dead organic matter and absorbing the released nutrients
questions.explanation: Saprotrophic fungi secrete extracellular enzymes to break down dead organic material (e.g. lignin, cellulose) and absorb the resulting simple compounds, playing a key role in decomposition and nutrient cycling.

questions.question: Fungi are particularly important decomposers of woody plant material because many species can produce enzymes capable of degrading:
questions.correct_answer: Lignin and cellulose
questions.explanation: White-rot and brown-rot fungi produce ligninolytic and cellulolytic enzymes (e.g. lignin peroxidase, cellulases) that few other organisms can produce, enabling them to decompose tough woody plant tissue.

questions.question: In the genetic study of fungi, a mating type locus in heterothallic fungi determines:
options: Compatibility for sexual reproduction, since mating typically occurs only between individuals of different mating types
The rate of spore germination only
questions.correct_answer: Compatibility for sexual reproduction, since mating typically occurs only between individuals of different mating types
questions.explanation: Heterothallic fungi require the fusion of hyphae from two individuals of different, genetically determined mating types (e.g. MAT1-1 and MAT1-2) to complete sexual reproduction, unlike homothallic (self-fertile) species.

questions.question: A fungus described as 'homothallic' is one that:
options: Can complete sexual reproduction using a single genetic individual (self-fertile), without needing a compatible mating partner
Requires two different mating types to reproduce sexually
questions.correct_answer: Can complete sexual reproduction using a single genetic individual (self-fertile), without needing a compatible mating partner
questions.explanation: Homothallic fungi are self-fertile, capable of undergoing sexual reproduction from a single strain, in contrast to heterothallic fungi which require partners of opposite, compatible mating type.

questions.question: Conidia, common asexual spores in many Ascomycota and their anamorphic (imperfect) states, are typically produced:
options: Exogenously (externally) at the tips or sides of specialised hyphae called conidiophores
Only after meiosis inside an ascus
By binary fission of a single cell
questions.correct_answer: Exogenously (externally) at the tips or sides of specialised hyphae called conidiophores
questions.explanation: Conidia are asexual, non-motile spores formed externally (exogenously) on conidiophores, distinguishing them from sporangiospores which develop endogenously inside a sporangium, as in many Zygomycota.

questions.question: The teleomorph of a fungus refers to its:
questions.correct_answer: Sexual (perfect) reproductive stage
questions.explanation: Teleomorph denotes the sexual state of a fungus, in contrast to the anamorph, which is the asexual (conidial) state; some fungi are known to have both states linked as a single pleomorphic species (holomorph).

questions.question: Which structural feature is typically used to distinguish Basidiomycota hyphae from those of Ascomycota under the microscope?
options: Presence of clamp connections at septa
Presence of a cell wall made of cellulose instead of chitin
questions.correct_answer: Presence of clamp connections at septa
questions.explanation: Clamp connections at hyphal septa are a distinctive feature commonly used to identify dikaryotic Basidiomycota mycelium, not typically found in Ascomycota, which have chitinous cell walls like all true fungi.
